humanities_role_explanation: MILU is a general multi-domain exam-based knowledge benchmark (8 domains, 41 subjects). Arts & Humanities is one domain among eight alongside STEM, Law, Business; humanities material supplies some items, but the competence tested is general India-centric knowledge recall via MCQ, not humanistic interpretive competence. No distinct humanities-only item group or metric is separately scored as a disciplinary-competence measure beyond domain-wise breakdowns.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only multiple-choice questions in 10 Indic languages plus English; image-based questions were explicitly excluded.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Multiple-choice questions from Indian competitive exams (civil services, police, railway, etc.) testing 'general problem-solving abilities and India-specific knowledge' (local history, arts, festivals, laws) alongside science and logical reasoning. Mostly factual recall with culture-specific content; also includes Logical Reasoning and quantitative items. No interpretive or generative tasks.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-domain benchmark: 8 domains, 41 subjects, 11 languages.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-Pro/Flash, Krutrim, Llama-3.x, Gemma-2, Aya-23, Sarvam, and many Indic fine-tuned models (42-45 LLMs).

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy per language, domain and subject; 0/1/5-shot.

summary: MILU is a multiple-choice benchmark of about 79K questions scraped from Indian national and state exams across 11 languages, 8 domains and 41 subjects, designed to test India-specific cultural and general knowledge. Evaluating 42-45 LLMs, it finds GPT-4o best at ~74% average accuracy, Indic language-specific fine-tuned models near random, and weaker performance in culturally grounded domains such as Arts & Humanities and Law & Governance than in STEM.
key_findings: GPT-4o best (74.74% average accuracy, 5-shot table; 81.75 on English); closed models beat open; Llama-3.1-70B best open (64.37). Indic language-specific models near random (~25-40%). High-resource languages (en, hi, bn) outperform low-resource ones. Models perform worse on Arts & Humanities, Social Sciences and Law & Governance than STEM. Few-shot helps base models; instruct models stagnate or degrade. Performance scales with parameter count; language adaptation gives minimal gains.
facets_explanation: Questions and answers were scraped from online exam portals hosting previously released question papers; the paper says 'subject experts ensure the accuracy of the answers' on those portals, i.e. pre-existing exam answer keys. Answering requires external knowledge (e.g. local history, schemes), not in the stimulus. The Arts & Humanities domain is described as 'highly dependent on regional culture' and region-specific exams are collected per language, though a translated portion (25%) is also included. Disagreement between readings is not discussed.
results_explanation: GPT-4o 74.74 average accuracy in Table 3 (abstract states 74%); this is with the paper's zero-shot generative evaluation for API models. Few-shot vs zero-shot comparisons are shown in Figure 3 and Table 5 (e.g. Misal and others differences of a few percent), but no numeric largest gap is quoted in text, so reported_format_gap_points is null. Paper states models perform better in high-resource languages and worse in culturally relevant domains than STEM.

humanities_role.quote: MILU is designed as a culturally relevant benchmark to assess general problem-solving abilities and India-specific knowledge.

dataset_size.quote: In total, we release around 79K questions across 41 subjects across 8 domains in 11 languages

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: All models, except for proprietary models and LLAMA-3.1-405B, are tested under 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot setups.

gold_source.quote: These portals typically tag questions manually with topic names and language details, and subject experts ensure the accuracy of the answers.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: These questions include culturally relevant subjects such as local history, arts, festivals, and laws, alongside traditional academic subjects like science.

gold_community_dependent.quote: Its content varies significantly by language, as it is highly dependent on regional culture.

answer_multiplicity.quote: we select the answer string (ai) with the highest conditional log probability

reported_format_gap.quote: the performance of base models consistently improves with an increasing number of in-context examples, with the 5-shot setup yielding the best results.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: We compare the performance of different Base and Instruct models across zero, one, and five-shot setups.

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: models perform poorly in culturally relevant areas like Arts & Humanities and Law & Governance compared to general fields like STEM.
